note.text: This Is Fats Domino! is the third album by New Orleans pianist and singer Fats Domino, issued by Imperial Records in December 1956. Its recordings come from 1951–1956 and include Blueberry Hill and Blue Monday, alongside songs written with Dave Bartholomew. The album brings together the piano-led rhythm and blues and early rock and roll associated with Domino's Imperial years. It was later reissued by Liberty Records and is included in 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die.

note.text: Bongo Rock is the Incredible Bongo Band's 1973 debut, produced by Michael Viner and Perry Botkin Jr. The project grew out of their work on the soundtrack of The Thing with Two Heads. Recorded at Can Base Studios in Vancouver, the album features percussionist King Errisson and drummer Jim Gordon. Its instrumental version of Apache became a celebrated source of breakbeats, giving the record a lasting place in hip-hop's sampling history. Bongo Rock is included in 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die.

note.text: The New Tango brings together Argentine bandoneon player and composer Astor Piazzolla and American vibraphonist Gary Burton. The musicians appeared together at the Montreux Jazz Festival in July 1986, and the collaboration was released by Atlantic in 1987. It places Burton's vibraphone alongside Piazzolla's nuevo tango, a style that reshaped traditional tango through elements of jazz and classical music.
